Duplicate of #58838

Purpose

Migrate the base RotaryEmbedding from a plain CustomOp to a vLLM IR op (vllm.ir.ops.rotary_embedding), so the QK-norm + RoPE(+KVCache) fusion patterns match a stable IR node without having to force custom_ops=["+rotary_embedding"].

This resolves the long-standing # TODO: support rope native forward match blocks in vllm/config/compilation.py and the underlying pattern-match failure tracked in #28042 (RoPE only matched the fusion when registered as a custom op). It follows the direction of #38756 ("Port RoPE ops to IR").

RoPE now emits the same IR node on every forward path (native/CUDA/HIP), so:

  • fusion patterns match regardless of custom_ops, and
  • the actual kernel (native vs. _C vs. AITER Triton) is chosen by IR op priority during lowering instead of a global custom-op flag.

Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

The prior effort — #43199 ([vLLM IR][Rope] Port RotaryEmbedding to IR Ops, @wxsIcey) and its predecessors #39488/#41773/#42264 — is closed and unmerged (last state: merge conflicts, mergeable_state: dirty), and RoPE is not an IR op on current main. This PR differs materially:

  • Rebased on current main and conflict-free.
  • Keeps MatcherRotaryEmbedding (making it emit the IR node) instead of deleting it. Current main gained QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass (the AITER QK-norm+RoPE+KVCache fusion, [Model][Hardware][AMD]: Part 1/2 -> Enable e2e QK Norm + RoPE + KV Cache runtime fusion for Qwen3-30B-A3B on ROCM_AITER_FA, and ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN #42749) after [vLLM IR][Rope] Port RotaryEmbedding to IR Ops #43199 was written, and that pass depends on the matcher — deleting it (as [vLLM IR][Rope] Port RotaryEmbedding to IR Ops #43199 did) would break the AITER fusion.
  • Completes the ROCm/AITER path: adds an aiter IR provider for rotary_embedding, decouples the AITER Triton dispatch from RotaryEmbedding.enabled(), and sets ROCm IR-op priority to prefer AITER when enabled. Removing the +rotary_embedding force otherwise silently disabled AITER RoPE on ROCm.
  • Scope is intentionally limited to the base RotaryEmbedding (Neox + GPT-J, full/partial rope). DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding, mRoPE, flashinfer, and the key=None cross-layer-KV-sharing path are left on their existing paths and can be ported in follow-ups.

ROCm/AITER) Cleanup | vllm/config/compilation.py | remove the three +rotary_embedding force-appends Test | tests/kernels/ir/test_rotary_embedding.py (new) | registration / native-vs-forward_static / provider dispatch / not-inplace / opcheck

Test plan

This is a draft. It has been static-checked only; it is not yet runtime-verified — I do not currently have a GPU/ROCm box available for this branch. The following must pass before this leaves draft:

# IR op unit tests (CUDA/ROCm)

# Fusion still matches WITHOUT +rotary_embedding (the point of #28042)
pytest tests/compile/passes/test_qk_norm_rope_fusion.py -v

  • Runtime: pending (draft) — unit/fusion tests above + a gsm8k parity run vs. the unfused baseline (this change alters the RoPE lowering path, so accuracy parity must be confirmed) will be added here before marking ready-for-review.

nodes.body: Kernel overhead measurement
Performance numbers: Compilation took 67.78 seconds on base versus 78.28 seconds on the PR, a one-time ~10 seconds startup cost

Dropping the fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache force-append turns off MRoPE fusion.
The pass only discovers MRoPE configs when is_custom_op_enabled("rotary_embedding") (qk_norm_rope_kvcache_fusion.py:852-856), and MatcherMRotaryEmbedding.forward_native raises. MRotaryEmbedding shares the CustomOp name, so with the #42749 recipe it now runs forward_native instead of torch.ops.vllm.mrope. Main resolves custom_ops to ['+rotary_embedding','none']; this PR gives ['none'] (checked CPU-only). #50212 measured +4.7–15.8% from this fusion. All MRoPE tests pin +rotary_embedding, so CI can't see it. Keep the force for MRoPE models (or warning_once) and add a +rms_norm MRoPE case.

This undoes #42833 for configs that only set a fusion flag. use_aiter still requires self.enabled(), so the gpt-oss MI3xx recipe gets no cos_sin_cache_bf16. +# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""vLLM IR ops for rotary positional embedding."""
+
+import torch
+from torch import Tensor
+

+
+def _rotate(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, is_neox: bool) -> Tensor:
+    """Rotate contiguous halves (NeoX) or interleaved pairs (GPT-J)."""
+    cos = cos.unsqueeze(-2).to(x.dtype)
+    sin = sin.unsqueeze(-2).to(x.dtype)
+
+    if is_neox:
+        x1, x2 = torch.chunk(x, 2, dim=-1)
+    else:
+        x1 = x[..., ::2]
+        x2 = x[..., 1::2]
+
+    o1 = x1 * cos - x2 * sin
+    o2 = x2 * cos + x1 * sin
+
+    if is_neox:
+        return torch.cat((o1, o2), dim=-1)
+    return torch.stack((o1, o2), dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+
+
+@register_op(activations=["query", "key"], allow_inplace=True)
+def rotary_embedding(
+    positions: Tensor,
+    query: Tensor,
+    key: Tensor,
+    head_size: int,
+    rotary_dim: int,
+    cos_sin_cache: Tensor,
+    is_neox: bool,
+) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
+    """Apply RoPE to query and key."""
+    positions = positions.flatten()
+    num_tokens = positions.shape[0]
+    cos_sin = cos_sin_cache.index_select(0, positions)
+    cos, sin = cos_sin.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+
+    query_shape = query.shape
+    query = query.view(num_tokens, -1, head_size)
+    query_rot = _rotate(query[..., :rotary_dim], cos, sin, is_neox)
+    query = torch.cat((query_rot, query[..., rotary_dim:]), dim=-1).reshape(query_shape)
+
+    key_shape = key.shape
+    key = key.view(num_tokens, -1, head_size)
+    key_rot = _rotate(key[..., :rotary_dim], cos, sin, is_neox)
+    key = torch.cat((key_rot, key[..., rotary_dim:]), dim=-1).reshape(key_shape)
+
+    return query, key
+
+
+rotary_embedding.override_tolerance(torch.float16, atol=5e-3, rtol=2e-3)
+rotary_embedding.override_tolerance(torch.bfloat16, atol=3e-2, rtol=2e-2)
